_comment: The golden corpus: hand-labelled expected results for every lab target.
AUTHORED FROM lab/corpus/ground-truth.sh — the software's own account of itself,
read by execing into the containers — and from the compose target definitions. NOT
from any scanner observation. corpus-check diffs the scanner's output AGAINST this;
the two sources never cross, so a passing check is not the scanner agreeing with
itself. Every label carries a `source` naming where the truth came from.
Ports scanned by the check: 21,22,23,80,443,631,8080,8443,9100. Port recall is over
the open ports in that set. A host reachable only behind a SYN-dropping filter is
labelled alive=false: a connect scan cannot distinguish it from absent, and pretending
otherwise would be labelling a capability the scanner does not have.

the rule ships (session 15) but the fingerprint TLS client offers only Go's secure cipher suites, so it never negotiates an insecure one and a weak-only server cannot even be handshaked. Measured: against nginx offering only ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256 the client's handshake fails. UNBLOCKER: inspectOnlyTLSConfig must OFFER the weak suites (the same way it offers old TLS versions via MinVersion) so a server that accepts one is detectable. An engine change, deferred from this lab/corpus session.
